# UIService

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- A **service**: get it with `game:GetService("UIService")`
- **Not creatable**: it cannot be created with `Instance.new`

The parent of every `ScreenGui`. It also provides the properties a layout needs about the screen, and the gamepad selection.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AutoSelect` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether the engine manages the selection when the game does not. When it is on and nothing is selected, the first press of a D-pad, a stick or an arrow key selects the first selectable object on the topmost screen, and a pointer press clears the selection, so a player who uses the mouse sees no selection outline. When it is off, the selection changes only when a script sets it. |
| `DisplayScale` | `number` | — | read-only | The ratio of the window's pixels to its logical size: 2 on a display at 200% scaling. UI coordinates are in pixels, so multiply by this value to give something the same physical size on different screens. |
| `GamepadId` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The id of the gamepad that can navigate the interface and activate `SelectedObject`. At 0, every gamepad can. With a positive id, only that gamepad navigates menus; the others still reach `InputService` and their `InputContext`s. Keyboard and pointer navigation are not affected. Changing the id releases any held navigation input. |
| `SafeAreaInsets` | `Rect` | — | read-only | The distance from each edge of the window within which drawing is not safe, in pixels, because of a camera cutout, rounded corners or a system gesture bar. It is zero for a desktop window. |
| `ScreenOrientation` | `Enum.ScreenOrientation` | `Enum.ScreenOrientation.LandscapeSensor` | read/write | The orientations in which the game can be held on a phone or tablet. Setting it takes effect immediately and rotates the screen if needed. The value saved with the scene is the one the game starts with. A layout sees the new `AbsoluteSize` on the next frame. It has no effect on a desktop. |
| `SelectedObject` | `UIObject?` | — | read/write | The UI object selected by a gamepad or the arrow keys, or nil. The D-pad, the left stick and the arrow keys move the selection: to the object's `NextSelectionUp`, `Down`, `Left` or `Right` if set, and otherwise to the nearest selectable object in that direction. `ButtonA` or Enter fires the selected object's `Activated`.<br><br>Set it to move the selection, for example to the first button when a menu opens. Raises an error for an object that is not `Selectable`. |
| `ViewportSize` | `Vector2` | — | read-only | The size of the area the interface is drawn into, in pixels: the window in a game, or the Viewport panel in the editor. `AbsolutePosition` and the pointer position are measured in it, and a `ScreenGui` with `ReferenceHeight` is scaled to it. |

## Methods

### `GetFocusedTextInput(): TextInput?`

Returns the `TextInput` that has keyboard focus, or nil. A chat hotkey can check it before opening the chat box.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `SelectionChanged(selected: UIObject?)`

Fires when `SelectedObject` changes. Passes the newly selected object, or nil.

### `TextInputFocusReleased(input: TextInput)`

Fires when a `TextInput` loses keyboard focus.

### `TextInputFocused(input: TextInput)`

Fires when a `TextInput` gains keyboard focus.
